subject: Problems when using Chinese charactesr with renderGvis

messages.author: 91c9897630bbc6e6
messages.subject: Problems when using Chinese charactesr with renderGvis
parts:
Hi.  Thanks for this awesome web framework for R.
The new renderGvis is extremely useful.   But it seems there is some problems with Chinese.

Here is the content of the demo files.   
ui.R

library(shiny)
library(googleVis)

# Define UI for application that plots random distributions 
shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
  
  # Application title
  headerPanel("Hello Shiny!"),
  
  # Sidebar with a slider input for number of observations
  sidebarPanel(
    
  ),
  
  # Show a plot of the generated distribution
  mainPanel(
    htmlOutput("cn"),
    htmlOutput("gvis1")
  )
))


---------------------
server.R

library(shiny)
library(googleVis)

shinyServer(function(input, output) { 
  
  output$cn <- renderUI( { 
    s = '中文测试'
    HTML(s)
  }) 
  
  output$gvis1 <- renderGvis({
    tmp = data.frame(cname=c("中文一","中文二"),ename=c("en1","en2"),count=c(15,20),stringsAsFactors=F)
    namestring = "ename"
    titlestring = "Count"
    #namestring = "cname"
    #titlestring = "中文Count"
    gvisPieChart(tmp[,c(namestring,"count")],
                 options=list(title=titlestring,
                              width = 800,
                              legend.position='top'))
  })
}) 

--------------------------

1. Now everything is OK.   Including the Chinese characters.
2. If uncomment the titlestring = "中文Count",  then all the Chinese characters in webpage become unrecognizable, no matter how to change the encoding settings in Chrome browser.
3. If uncomment the namestring = "cname", then there is no output.  It seems there is  an Uncaught SyntaxError: Unexpected token \ in Shiny.js : 575 reported by the Chrome browser's webpage inspector.

Any suggestion would be welcome.  Thanks in advance.

Yun F.
